answer: Divergent History Auditing. Each identity publishes a slow hash chain of its actions, timestamped at a fixed cadence. Clones share one lineage and cannot fork it without colliding on chain state, so divergence is detectable like a crack in a glacier. Auditors swap chain heads off-band via whisper channels each cycle and flag any identity whose history branches. An attacker must run separate compute and storage per clone, sustaining full chain replication through every dawn, making each additional identity cost a full independent node rather than a cheap alias.
